{{Ship module infobox}}

The '''Frame Shift Wake Scanner''' is a Class 0 scanner utility fitted to a ship's utility mounts. It analyses the High Energy Wake left when another ship jumps to a different star system, revealing the departing commander and destination system. Completing a wake scan can also yield encoded data used in [[Engineering]].<ref name="ed-wiki-wake">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Frame_Shift_Wake_Scanner Elite Dangerous Wiki: ''Frame Shift Wake Scanner''], revision of 23 November 2024. Current community description, usage, standard variants, Engineering options, and encoded wake-data family; retrieved 15 September 2026.</ref>

== Operation ==

Assign the scanner to a fire group, deploy hardpoints, target a High Energy Wake, and remain within the scanner's rated range. Hold the assigned trigger while keeping the wake inside the scanning arc. Every unmodified rating takes 10 seconds to complete a scan; the destination and wake data are returned only after the scan finishes.<ref name="edcd-wake">[https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EDCD/coriolis-data/9e5273b56426596061e2b02a6ba53e3e4103c9ab/modules/hardpoints/frame_shift_wake_scanner.json EDCD Coriolis data: ''Frame Shift Wake Scanner''], pinned module-data revision committed 6 June 2024. Standard rating, mass, integrity, power, range, scan-time, and price records; retrieved 15 September 2026.</ref>

The scanner identifies where the ship went; it does not move the scanning ship or bypass the normal jump-range, fuel, permit, or route requirements. A commander following the wake must still align with and engage the [[Frame Shift Drive]] for the destination.

== Standard variants ==

All standard variants occupy one utility mount, have Class 0 size and 1.3-tonne mass, and complete an unmodified scan in 10 seconds. Higher ratings extend the scan range while sharply increasing power draw.<ref name="edcd-wake" />

== Encoded wake data ==

A successful High Energy Wake scan may award one of the five encoded materials in the wake-scans family:<ref name="ed-wiki-wake" />

* Atypical Disrupted Wake Echoes — Grade 1;
* Anomalous FSD Telemetry — Grade 2;
* Strange Wake Solutions — Grade 3;
* Eccentric Hyperspace Trajectories — Grade 4;
* Datamined Wake Exceptions — Grade 5.

These materials are stored as encoded [[Engineering Materials|Engineering data]]. The scanner is therefore useful both for identifying a departing ship's destination and for gathering data used by Frame Shift Drive and other blueprints.

== Engineering ==

Frame Shift Wake Scanners accept six standard blueprints and no Experimental Effects:<ref name="inara-wake-engineering">INARA: [https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/167/ ''Frame Shift Wake Scanner — Fast scan''], [https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/168/ ''Long range''], and [https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/169/ ''Wide angle'']. Current blueprint effects and grade records; retrieved 15 September 2026.</ref>

* '''Fast scan''' reduces scan time at the cost of range and integrity.
* '''Lightweight''' reduces mass at the cost of integrity.
* '''Long range''' extends range while increasing power draw and narrowing the scan angle.
* '''Reinforced''' increases integrity at the cost of mass.
* '''Shielded''' increases integrity at the cost of power draw.
* '''Wide angle''' expands the scanning arc at the cost of mass and scan time.

The useful choice depends on the ship's purpose. Fast scan shortens the time spent holding a wake in the reticle, long range permits acquisition from farther away, and lightweight reduces the module's effect on a range-sensitive build.

== Acquisition ==

Standard E–A variants are normal credit-purchased utility modules. Availability depends on the current Outfitting stock at a station, surface port, or carrier service.
